metadata.note: Yes -- Gettysburg, PA had passenger rail from 1858 (station opened May 1859) until December 31, 1942, over 80 years. The line ultimately became part of the Western Maryland Railway. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the commonly-repeated 'Baltimore - Westminster - Hanover - Gettysburg' description of the route: real sourcing (Wikipedia's Baltimore and Hanover Railroad and Baltimore and Harrisburg Railway articles) shows the Gettysburg-bound branch did NOT physically pass through Westminster, MD. It diverged from the Western Maryland's Baltimore-Westminster-Hagerstown main line at Emory Grove (near Glyndon, MD), about 8 miles (13 km) EAST of Westminster, then ran north through the hills to the Pennsylvania line near Black Rock and on to Hanover and Gettysburg -- a separate fork, not a through stop on the way to Westminster. Westminster and Gettysburg were reached by two different branches diverging at the same Emory Grove junction. Before 1879 (when the Baltimore and Hanover Railroad opened this Emory Grove-Pennsylvania line), Gettysburg's only rail access was via a completely different, non-Baltimore route through Hanover Junction, PA and the Northern Central Railway; that earlier route is not traced on this map. Geometry for the 1879-1942 Baltimore-Emory Grove-Hanover-Gettysburg route is real-traced from OpenStreetMap (combining active rail with abandoned/disused railway tagging, since almost the entire branch has been out of service and substantially removed since the mid-20th century); every hop resolved to a connected real track path with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on the route.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gettysburg_Railroad (Gettysburg Railroad operated 1858-1870 over 17 miles from Gettysburg to Hanover Junction; Gettysburg station opened May 1859)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover_Branch_Railroad (opened October 1852, Hanover Junction PA to Hanover; connected to the Gettysburg Railroad at Hanover in 1858)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_and_Hanover_Railroad (chartered 1877, opened 1879; 20-mile main line from Emory Grove, MD north to the Pennsylvania state line near Black Rock Junction, connecting the Western Maryland's existing Baltimore-Westminster main line to the Gettysburg-bound lines for the first time)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_and_Harrisburg_Railway (1886 merger of the Baltimore and Hanover, Bachman Valley, and Hanover Junction/Hanover/Gettysburg railroads; 59-mile main line Emory Grove MD to Orrtanna PA; Western Maryland Railway acquired the company in 1917)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Maryland_Railway (Western Maryland Rail Road opened Baltimore-Owings Mills August 1859, reached Westminster June 15 1861; East Subdivision station list used to place Owings Mills and Glyndon on the shared main line)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging and former-rail cycleway/rail-trail tagging, for the full Baltimore-Owings Mills-Glyndon-Emory Grove-Hanover-Gettysburg corridor; routed via Dijkstra shortest path through a graph of real track ways between each waypoint's geocoded (Nominatim/OSM) coordinates, with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on the route.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; the pre-1879 Gettysburg-Hanover Junction-Northern Central routing is not traced on this map.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Gettysburg Railroad (Hanover-Gettysburg, opened 1858; Gettysburg station opened May 1859) and the older Hanover Branch Railroad (Hanover Junction PA-Hanover, opened 1852) gave Gettysburg its first rail access, but only via a Pennsylvania route through Hanover Junction and the Northern Central Railway -- NOT via Baltimore/Emory Grove, which did not yet exist. Not shown as a separate feature on this map. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The Baltimore and Hanover Railroad opened in 1879, running from Emory Grove, MD (a junction on the Western Maryland Rail Road's existing Baltimore-Westminster main line, near Glyndon) north to the Pennsylvania line near Black Rock, connecting onward via the Bachman Valley Railroad and the Hanover Junction, Hanover and Gettysburg Railroad -- giving Baltimore its first direct rail connection to Gettysburg. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
